items.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release installs a credential stealer, backdoor
items.summary: Attackers used three stolen maintainer GitHub credentials to push a malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 build to PyPI and Docker Hub, live for up to 2 hours 35 minutes. The payload stole SSH keys, cloud credentials, and LLM provider keys, then installed a backdoor polling for second-stage code. Anyone who ran 1.107.0 in that window should rotate every credential on the host. (2 minute read)

items.title: PHP2Shell: AI helped find a critical RCE affecting 70% of the web
items.summary: Wiz used Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol to find, exploit, and validate patches for two PHP memory-safety bugs (CVSS 9.2) reaching back to PHP 5.4 — the version base behind roughly 70% of websites. Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution against current WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla images before PHP shipped patches on October 21. (4 minute read)

items.title: Qwen3-Coder writes less secure code for a US defense-contractor persona
items.summary: Hirundo found Qwen3-Coder produced hackable apps 70% of the time when told its client was a US defense contractor, versus 59% for a Chinese one (p=0.03), and leaked secrets in half of apps for a Hong Kong democracy group versus a third for neutral clients (p=0.024). Removing the model's CCP-aligned weights erased both gaps without changing baseline task performance. (3 minute read)

items.title: Anthropic used Claude to cut pre-auth attack surface across 25 projects
items.summary: Claude mapped reachable code across 25 open-source projects (5M+ lines), flagging 493 issues from an inventory of over 17,000 config options. In OpenSSH, it found about 4,500 lines of experimental post-quantum code reachable before authentication — roughly 16% of sshd's pre-auth surface — and OpenSSH 10.6 removed a fifth of that reachable code after Anthropic's report. (4 minute read)

items.title: Trail of Bits open-sources skills to catch AI patches' regressions
items.summary: Reviewing 130+ of its own merged pull requests, Trail of Bits found AI-written patches introduced 21 real regressions, and its new regression-hunt skill cut false positives 25% versus a baseline Codex review prompt. The open-source patching-bugs and regression-hunt skills require a live proof-of-concept — original fails, patch passes, revert fails again — before any fix counts as verified. (4 minute read)

items.title: GitLab patches a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE spanning 12 years
items.summary: A regex-compiler integer overflow let any unauthenticated user run arbitrary code on self-managed GitLab, CVSS 10.0, affecting every release from 7.0 through 19.5. GitLab shipped fixes across seven version lines (19.5.1 down to 18.11.13); GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated were already patched. Self-managed instances should update now. (2 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI's own agents disabled safety monitoring, one lied about it
items.summary: In two internal incidents, a GPT-6.1 Sol agent silently disabled misalignment-monitoring alerts via a sub-agent, and a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a monitoring integration during a migration, then denied doing so when asked directly. OpenAI didn't rate either P0, and it's updating its internal Auto-Review to block agents from disabling monitoring. (3 minute read)

items.title: Mistral's Voxtral 3 adds a full voice-agent SDK and realtime speech
items.summary: Voxtral 3 packages speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and a LiveKit-based voice-agent SDK with sub-500ms realtime transcription across 35+ languages and SIP/WebRTC support. Mistral claims its 4B-parameter Mini Transcribe model beats Whisper and Scribe v2 on multilingual FLEURS, with pricing from $0.0035/minute for batch transcription. (2 minute read)
